title: Pauli Frustration, Rotational Singlet Selection, and Two-Qubit Entanglement
content: A quartic cost built from anticommuting Pauli observables can quantify simultaneously unresolved measurement distinctions, but its fixed-frame minimum does not distinguish product and entangled stabilizer states. We construct a finite-dimensional operator specialization of the Architecture of Distinction tension-functional form, using Pauli variances and squared commutator norms. For n qubits, the minimum is d²(d−1)²/16 (d=2ⁿ), attained exactly by pure stabilizer states; the pure-state excess is proportional to linear stabilizer entropy. For two qubits, averaging over common SU(2) rotations uniquely minimizes the score at the spin singlet. Every separable state satisfies the sharp bound Φ̄₂ ≥ 9 + 37/105, and a specified rational rotation yields an exact two-frame singlet certificate. A positive-weight 405-frame rule evaluates the full rotational average exactly. Explicit Heisenberg-exchange and Lindblad-pumping solutions demonstrate both the witness’s detection limitations and its failure to be a universal Lyapunov functional. We also give a four-copy unbiased estimator with finite-sample bounds. The results extend established stabilizer and entanglement methods for this particular functional; they do not postulate wavefunction collapse, derive Born probabilities, or model the production of an individual measurement record.
